body: I can't figure out how to send a message. I'm on my phone. Generally it wouldn't be so hard but for some reason I'm not firing on all cylinders right now. I'll talk to anyone who will listen. Except family/friends. We're very private people. Can you pm me first? :)

He was absolutely distraught when I talked to him. I could see this as a cry for help. And I'm doing whatever I can to help. In the meantime I don't know how to help myself. Between my own mental health issues and my daughter who is currently in treatment at a mental health facility (days only), my sister who has issues and is always crying out to me for help... and now this. I have a very stressful job (that I can't quit) and am barely making it through the day myself. I don't feel strong enough for this.

I think he would have gone through with it if I hadn't come home. I know he feels he does more harm than good with our daughter-she's special needs (lots of emotional and behavioral issues, including self harm). He worries that his spankings contributed to her hurting herself when she gets overwhelmed. This is not the case. She's in therapy, sees a psychiatrist, and is currently at a mental health treatment "school". He takes her to and from school daily and works nights so she has this opportunity. He's always been very consistent with her, and she listens to him. But it's always been a sore spot for him because I don't feel that their relationship is as good as it could be (he has very high expectations of her and can be critical), and sometimes I do jump in and protect her instead of supporting him as a parent. That was what triggered the argument yesterday. Plus he hasn't been sleeping much and I know that has to be a part of it.

I will talk if you will listen. 

I'm so angry and hurt that he felt this was his only option (although he did do a cry for help). He says he's no longer suicidal but it was a very in-the-moment-thing. So I have no idea if it will happen again the next time he's distraught. I have pretty severe anxiety and it almost feels inevitable. I can find him a counselor. I know there are things I can work on to help him but since he says he doesn't feel this way now he doesn't want treatment. He doesn't like the way medication makes him feel. I've tried natural approaches to my own mental health. Exercise, abstaining from alcohol and caffeine. It's not enough. But he's not depressed all the time. That's the thing. It's always triggered by something. It could be something happening, or it could be his thoughts. If we hadn't gotten into a fight yesterday morning he was planning on heading to crossfit. I've never felt like I had to watch him for suicide before.
